subject: Re: Dark-launch plan for new EU subprocessor + transfer scoping
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@arcadiahealth.com>
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference.com
Cc: Emily Turner <legal@arcadiahealth.com>, privacy@arcadiahealth.com
Date: 2026-07-18T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Scope question: adding EU subprocessor for inference cache (dark-launch)

Hi Hannah,

Quick question as we're mapping our onboarding tasks: Arcadia is planning a pilot that will route token-level cache traffic to a specialized EU-based subprocessor run by Redwood's partner. We want to understand the transfer boundary implications for our DPA/SCCs and whether a dark-launch (limited traffic, 10% of requests) changes the procurement or IDTA/UK Addendum obligations.

Attached is a one-page diagram of the proposed flow and a short list of control expectations. Can you loop in the right folks on your side so we can confirm whether Arcadia needs a separate TIA/DTIA or if the existing SCC mapping + onshore fallback suffices?

Thanks,
Sanjay Rao
Director, Cloud Integrations
Arcadia Health
Attachments: flow_diagram_v1.pdf (diagram), control-expectations.txt
From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference.com
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@arcadiahealth.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com, marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com, jonas_weber@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2026-07-18T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Scope question: adding EU subprocessor for inference cache (dark-launch)

Thanks Sanjay — good kickoff note. I think we can handle this as a scoped DTIA (short-lived) combined with targeted subprocessor attestation, but a few clarifications first:

- Is the data in the cache pseudonymized/hashed or plaintext tokens? (This impacts whether we treat it as personal data flows.)
- Will Arcadia need guaranteed residency for the cache (i.e., no fallback to non-EU regions)?
- Expected duration of the dark-launch (2–6 weeks?) and traffic % (you mentioned ~10%).

I've looped in Kimberly for legal redline guidance and Marissa for procurement triggers and SOW/contract timing. Jonas from infra will weigh in on routing/fallback mechanics.

Next steps proposed:
1) We (Redwood) fill out a DTIA scoping matrix (I attached the template) and mark fallback/residency options.
2) Legal (Kimberly) confirms whether the existing SCC mapping + UK Addendum needs an explicit amendment or a one-off TIA.
3) Procurement (Marissa) advises on timing for a subprocessor addendum and whether a short ride-along clause can be used for the dark launch.

I attached a DTIA-scoping-matrix.xlsx draft (internal). Happy to hop on a 30m sync if that's faster.

— Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Privacy Program Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: DTIA-scoping-matrix.xlsx
From: kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference.com
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@arcadiahealth.com>, Emily Turner <legal@arcadiahealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com
Date: 2026-07-19T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Scope question: adding EU subprocessor for inference cache (dark-launch)

Hannah / Sanjay — high level from legal:

1) If the cached tokens are personal data or can be reconstituted to personal data, Arcadia will need an explicit DTIA/TIA amendment to the DPA (we can scope it as a limited-scope DTIA tied to the pilot). If tokens are hashed/irreversibly pseudonymized prior to leaving Arcadia, we can likely treat it as non-personal in the DTIA scope, but need artefacts.

2) UK IDTA / UK Addendum: If Arcadia has UK-resident data in scope, we also need to confirm whether the UK Addendum changes the subprocessor notice process — usually notice + 30 days for customers, but a short pilot can be handled as an exception with documented mitigations.

3) Redlines: I reviewed Arcadia's requested changes (emailed separately). For a dark-launch carveout we can offer a timeboxed SOW amendment + operational attestation from the subprocessor. We should not add a permanent residency guarantee for the pilot.

Action items for Redwood legal (assign):
- Produce a slim DTIA amendment template (timeboxed) and a customer-facing attestation checklist.
- Provide written evidence of subprocessor technical controls (encryption-in-transit/at-rest, key custody, access logs) — we can include a redacted subprocessor report.

I'll attach a draft redlines_dpa_v3.docx and mark the pilot clauses. Sanjay / Emily — please review and flag must-haves.

— Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redlines_dpa_v3.docx
From: marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com
To: hannah_schmitt@redwood.inference.com, kimberly_park@redwood.inference.com
Cc: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@arcadiahealth.com>
Date: 2026-07-20T13:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Scope question: adding EU subprocessor for inference cache (dark-launch)

Team / Sanjay — procurement notes:

- If Arcadia signs a DTIA amendment, procurement will treat the pilot as a low-level change; we can onboard the subprocessor under a one-off addendum if the legal team signs off on the attestation. Typical procurement lead time: 10 business days after legal ok + internal security attestation.
- Pricing: a marginal subprocessor onboarding fee (one-time) + monitoring add-on. I'll draft an addendum template that includes an explicit rollback clause (automatic failback to onshore processing if any evidence of data leakage or control gaps).
- DocuSign cadence: we can wrap the amendment and SOW into a single envelope. Link to draft doc in Drive.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference
Attachments: subprocessor-dark-launch-checklist.pdf

Subject: Re: Scope question: adding EU subprocessor for inference cache (dark-launch)

Thanks all — appreciate the clarity. Quick confirmations from Arcadia side:

- Tokens will be pseudonymized (SHA-256) before transfer; we will provide a proof-of-process and sample logs.
- We do not require strict residency guarantees for the pilot but we do require documented rollback procedures and notification within 24 hours of any control exception.
- Pilot duration: 3 weeks, traffic ~8–12%.

Emily (legal) and I will review Kimberly's redlines and return comments by Friday. Let's aim to have the slim DTIA amendment + procurement checklist ready next week so we can launch the dark test week of July 27.

— Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Director, Cloud Integrations
Arcadia Health
